clue.text: Broken wind instrument finally replaced by daughter

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the instrument as the one to be swapped out
replaced by says one letter makes way for another in the same slot

blocks.note: a brass instrument
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wind instrument has been damaged, and the daughter has stepped in for the final part.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to trump is to fart, so TRUMPED means has broken wind; 'Broken wind instrument' wants to be read as one damaged trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump is everyday British slang for passing gas, so the past participle describes someone who has farted.

clue.text: National symbol incorporating hearts and spades separately in heading

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of a word, here two single letters placed apart

blocks.note: a heading at the top of a page is its title
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A national emblem is shown with card suits on a page heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' tells you the two suit letters go into different gaps of the heading word rather than side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is the floral emblem of Scotland, a national symbol.

clue.text: Subject to series of profound errors

indicators.note: a series runs on unbroken across the following words, so the letters are found inside that run

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of making a string of serious mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be under something, such as orders or review, is to be subject to it.

clue.text: Pities suspect caught embracing girl that's upset and gloomy

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters cannot be trusted in their printed order
in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the word is turned the other way
embracing means holding something in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a miss is a girl or young woman
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone feels pity, is caught holding a distressed girl, and grows gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of Pities are split around the turned-round girl, and the cricket C finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimistic person expects the worst, which is a gloomy outlook.

clue.text: Drop key objective introduced by Democrat

indicators.note: introduced by means the following element comes first, opening the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat
the Escape key on a computer keyboard
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A Democrat brings in a plan to drop a key goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a musical key or something important, but it is the computer key ESC.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to go down, a verb synonym of drop.

clue.text: Move down and remove bad marks?

blocks.note: first meaning: to put someone in a lower rank
second meaning, read whimsically: take away motes, little specks or blemishes

explanation.surface: A pupil is moved down a set and has poor marks taken off the record.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up sense: DE- as in removing, plus MOTE, a speck of dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote is to reduce someone's rank; split as de-mote it jokingly means clearing away specks.

clue.text: Regularly advised to stop working

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is often told by advisers to take a break from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or battery that dies has failed, meaning it has ceased to function.

clue.text: Vile male has the power to control monarch no longer

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it in one's grip, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
someone who has the power to act is able to do so
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, a monarch who reigns no more

explanation.surface: A wicked man seizes power over a deposed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a common crossword abbreviation for the Queen; 'no longer' fits since her reign has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable can mean wretched or contemptible, close in sense to vile, as in a miserable wretch.

clue.text: Trampled rodent running around middle of landing

indicators.note: a running animal is darting about, so its letters are scattered into a new order
middle of keeps only the central letter of the seven-letter word
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the central one

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A mouse scampers about a staircase landing, getting stamped on.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden is the past participle of tread, meaning walked on or trampled.

clue.text: Tip of nose surrounded by clear skin

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its leading letter, so only that is kept
surrounded by means enclosed, so the single letter goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: to rid a place is to clear it
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A beauty note: the end of your nose is ringed by clear skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin of fruit, cheese or bacon.

clue.text: Delay payment to people no longer working in South America?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for South
the United States

blocks.clueFragment: payment to people no longer working
blocks.note: money paid regularly to retired people

explanation.surface: A government in South America holds back money owed to retirees.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as an American retirement payment, a 'US pension' in the South; the question mark covers that fanciful split.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a temporary stop or postponement, as in a suspension of payments, so it means a delay.

clue.text: Backing singers admire characteristic of famous diva?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: rats are informers, who 'sing' to the police
to like someone is to think well of them

explanation.surface: Backing singers look up to the lead diva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing singers' reads as a pop term for the support vocalists, but backing is the reversal and the singers are informers.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous diva is a star, so something typical of her is like a star in manner.

clue.text: Laugh at revolutionary socialist vision falling short

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is spun to face the other way
falling short means not quite reaching the end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: red is the colour and nickname of left-wing socialists
an idea or vision of how things could be

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a revolutionary leftist whose grand plan fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary socialist' reads as one phrase about a radical, but revolutionary is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, which is to laugh at someone scornfully.

clue.text: Put off by night club saying you are old

indicators.note: saying means speaking, so the words are taken by their spoken sound as letters

blocks.note: a club for dancing at night
the letter U is pronounced like this word, as in text-speak
the letter R is pronounced like this word
aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone is deterred from going out when a nightclub tells them they are too old.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discouraged is to be deterred or dissuaded, which is what put off means here.

clue.text: Ancient city - one having new area with restricted parking

indicators.note: restricted means hemmed in, so the parking letter is confined within the other piece

blocks.note: the Indian city whose capital district is New Delhi
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A historic city, now with a new district, has limited parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One having new area' is a cryptic description: Delhi is a city that includes an area called New Delhi.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was an ancient Greek city, home to the famous oracle of Apollo.

clue.text: Job estimate includes start of renting flat out

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
includes means takes in, so the single letter goes inside the longer piece

blocks.note: a post is a job or position
to rate is to estimate or assess
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A quote for a job includes the first rent payment on a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment to rent, but 'flat out' is the definition: lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrate means lying stretched out face down, so a prostrate person is lying flat out.

clue.text: British nudists surprisingly refuse to go here

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something unexpected has happened, so the letters turn up in a new order

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written

explanation.surface: British naturists unexpectedly decline to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, the nudists declining, but it is the noun: rubbish. A dustbin is the British word for a garbage can.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustbins are containers for rubbish, the place household refuse is put.

clue.text: Shot went quickly round short course

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the final letter of the word is dropped
round means encircling, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: sped is the past tense of speed
a route is a course taken

explanation.surface: A runner dashed around a shortened track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like firing a gun, but it is the plant sense: shot up, put out new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has shot has put out new growth, which is to say it sprouted.

clue.text: Penthouses may supply money for Bill

indicators.note: houses as a verb means gives a home to, so one piece holds the other inside it
supply here is the adverb from supple, so the letters bend into a new shape

blocks.note: read as two words, Pent houses: the first half is taken as written and the second half is the container signal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Selling luxury top-floor flats may raise funds to settle a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Penthouses splits into Pent and houses; the letters of may go inside Pent, and the result is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment is money handed over to settle a bill or invoice.

clue.text: Policy behind last month's worsening performance

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this element is placed second

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December, the year's final month
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A company blames a policy for last month's poor results.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is a gradual deterioration, such as a worsening in results or performance.

clue.text: Seoul reportedly hosts games in public

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the word is taken by its sound
a host takes guests in, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: the capital of South Korea sounds like sole, which means only
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: The South Korean capital puts on sporting events for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school lesson often called games in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly means doing it without concealment, in public view.

clue.text: Less serious match?

blocks.note: first meaning: comparative of light, as in light entertainment
second meaning: a device for igniting a flame, which a match also is

explanation.surface: A fixture of lower importance, perhaps a friendly game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture; the question mark marks it as an example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter is the comparative of light, meaning more frivolous, and also a device for lighting cigarettes, much as a match is.

clue.text: Visionary king spared in author's criticism

indicators.note: spared means let off, so that letter is excused from the word and dropped

blocks.note: the setter, as author, refers to themself in the first person
stick is harsh criticism, as in taking stick
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A writer's review lets off a far-sighted ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the author is the setter, so author's gives MY. 'Taking stick' is British for receiving criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystic is a person who seeks spiritual truth through visions or insight, so a visionary.

clue.text: Hotel moved during generation of map for old city

indicators.note: moved means shifted from its place, so that letter is taken out first
during means within the span of, so the letter goes back inside at a new point

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a chart is a map, especially for sailors
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: A hotel is relocated while a new map of an ancient city is drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words for map and generation make CHARTAGE; the hotel letter then shifts three places along.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was an ancient North African city, the great rival of Rome.

clue.text: They work and work around the clock

blocks.note: first meaning: manual labourers, as in farm workers
second meaning: the pointers that move round a clock face

explanation.surface: Tireless staff who labour day and night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around the clock' wants to mean nonstop; read literally, it is where the second sense goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are workers, as in all hands on deck, and also the pointers on a clock face.

clue.text: Non-payment of fine beginning to get adult in trouble

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
in trouble means in a mess, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Not paying a fine starts to land a grown-up in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Defaulting is failing to meet a payment obligation, so it names non-payment.

clue.text: Allow event generating more output from the server

definitions.text: event generating more output from the server

blocks.note: first meaning: to permit

blocks.clueFragment: event generating more output from the server
blocks.note: second meaning: in tennis, a serve clipping the net that must be replayed

explanation.surface: Permission is sought for something that makes a computer server produce more data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' reads as a computer, but it is the tennis player serving, who gets another serve after this call.
explanation.definitionFit: To let is to allow; in tennis a let is a serve that touches the net and is taken again.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, F or G

blocks.clueFragment: A, B, C, D, F or G
blocks.note: surface reading: a run of letters, or grades, from the alphabet

blocks.clueFragment: A, B, C, D, F or G
blocks.note: setter's reading: each is a musical pitch name, and each is also anything other than the one missing letter of the musical alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The musical scale uses A to G; the list leaves out E, so the answer is both a musical term and, split 3-1, a statement that it is not that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each letter from A to G names a musical pitch, which is to say each is a single tone in written music.

clue.text: Provide evidence for visiting Lord's perhaps

blocks.note: someone visiting a place is at it
Lord's, the London cricket ground, hosts Test matches

explanation.surface: A witness speaks up for a nobleman they called on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's looks like a nobleman's possession, but it is the famous London cricket ground; 'perhaps' marks a Test as one example of what it stages.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest to something is to bear witness to it, giving proof or testimony.

clue.text: Abrupt rudeness upset client

indicators.note: abrupt means cut off suddenly, so the word loses its final letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A customer is offended by a curt, rude reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrupt rudeness' reads as one phrase about a brusque manner, but abrupt trims the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An end-user is the customer who finally uses a product, so a client of the supplier.
